additions.description: GET /api/articles supports filtering by 'author' query parameter but does not support filtering by 'tag' or 'favorited' parameters
additions.reasoning: The specification requires filtering articles by tag (e.g., GET /api/articles?tag=javascript) and favorited status, but the code only implements filtering by author.

additions.description: GET /api/articles supports 'offset' query parameter for pagination
additions.reasoning: The specification requires pagination with limit and offset, which is implemented, but the specification only explicitly mentions limit and offset in some tests; the code supports offset generally.

additions.description: The code returns 422 status code with detailed error messages for user registration uniqueness violations instead of 400 with 'Username and email must be unique' message
additions.reasoning: The specification expects 400 status and a message 'Username and email must be unique' on duplicate username or email, but the code returns 422 with separate error messages for username and email.

additions.description: The code returns 422 status code with 'Missing fields' error on incomplete user registration payload instead of 400
additions.reasoning: The specification does not specify 422 for missing fields, but the code uses 422 which is stricter than the specification's vague error expectations.

additions.description: The code returns 401 with error detail {'errors': {'body': ['email or password is invalid']}} on login failure instead of 401 with no specific message format required by specification
additions.reasoning: The specification requires 401 on login failure but does not specify exact error message format; the code provides a specific error message which is an addition.

additions.description: The code allows any authenticated user to update or delete any article regardless of ownership
additions.reasoning: The specification notes a security vulnerability that any user can update/delete any article; this is an addition as it is not a required behavior.

additions.description: The code returns 200 with empty object {} on GET /api/articles/{slug} for deleted articles instead of 404
additions.reasoning: The specification states the implementation returns 200 with empty object for deleted articles; this is an addition as typical REST APIs return 404.

additions.description: The code returns 200 with {'status': 'ok'} on DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{id} instead of 200 with empty object or no content
additions.reasoning: The specification does not specify the exact response body for comment deletion; the code returns a status message which is an addition.

omissions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug} does not validate that only the article owner can delete the article

omissions.description: POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments does not validate presence of comment body

omissions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{id} does not validate that only the comment author can delete the comment
omissions.reasoning: The specification does not explicitly require ownership check for comment deletion, but security best practices imply it; the code allows any authenticated user to delete any comment.
